newsitem.title: DENMARK: Lehman Bros ups Heineken to outperform.
newsitem.headline: Lehman Bros ups Heineken to outperform.

text.p: U.S. investment bank Lehman Brothers on Tuesday upgraded its assessment of Dutch brewer Heineken, to outperform citing its response to a campaign by competitor Anheuser-Busch and the stronger dollar.

A report by the bank, seen in Denmark where competitor Carlsberg is based, said that Heineken sought to speed its supplies by weeks rather than days to counter a "fresh beer" campaign by Anheuser-Busch's Budweiser brand.
The report did not say what the previous rating for Heineken was.
It also said that competition from micro-brewers appeared to be falling off as there were too many brands and too little brand support.
"Thirdly, while Heineken may not get any price increases in the U.S. the rise in the U.S. dollar will more than compensate over the next few years," it added.
"We continue to have some concerns about European beer shipments but the valuation of Heineken is getting increasingly compelling," Lehman Brothers concluded.
Heineken's share stood at 328.50 guilders on the Amsterdam bourse on Tuesday, 2.20 up from Monday's close. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
